Pimento 0.2.0 lets AI agents work with your PIM roles, keeps roles alive through the working day,
tells you when a new version is out, and adds Raycast and Alfred launchers.

## Highlights

- **AI agents (MCP)**: `pimento mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server for Claude Code, Claude
  Desktop, Cursor and other clients. It is read-only by default. With `--allow-activate` an agent
  can activate, end and renew roles, but each request is shown to you and sent only after you
  confirm it. Owner and the access administrator roles also need `--allow-privileged`.
- **Keep alive**: mark active roles or a preset, and Pimento renews them shortly before they expire,
  during your working hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 by default). Roles that need approval are never
  renewed, and a role you end early stays ended. On Linux, Windows and servers, `pimento
  keep-alive` runs the same rules in the foreground.
- **Update check**: once a day the app asks GitHub for the latest release and shows a one-line
  notice when there is a newer one. Nothing is downloaded or installed automatically. On the
  command line, `pimento version --check` asks.
- **Raycast and Alfred**: search, activate and end roles and presets from Raycast (*Search PIM
  Roles*, *Activate PIM Preset*, *Active PIM Roles*) or Alfred (the `pim` keyword). Both run the
  installed `pimento` and are installed from this repository (see `integrations/`).
- **Windows**: `pimento login` signs in through the browser, as on macOS and Linux
  (`--device-code` still works). `pimento completions powershell` provides completions for Windows
  PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, and `install.ps1` adds them to your profile.
- **Tenant badges**: each tenant shows as its initials on its own colour in the picker, toolbar
  and menu bar. *Settings › General › Fetch tenant logos* (off by default) shows the tenant's
  sign-in logo or website icon instead.
- `--id` and `--preset-id` select exactly one role or preset, for scripts.

**Not yet tested against a live tenant:** the keep-alive hand-over and browser sign-in on Windows.
The hand-over follows Microsoft's documentation and is tested against the demo simulator; the
Windows sign-in is tested in CI on Windows, without a real tenant. If PIM refuses the hand-over, Pimento activates the role again once it has ended, which leaves a
gap of seconds to minutes. If browser sign-in fails on Windows, use `pimento login --device-code`.

The full list is in the [changelog](https://github.com/Melvin2306/pimento/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Upgrading from 0.1.0

- **The app**: 0.1.0 has no update check, so download
  **[Pimento.dmg](https://github.com/Melvin2306/pimento/releases/latest/download/Pimento.dmg)** and
  drag Pimento onto Applications to replace the old app. Your settings, presets, history and
  sign-in stay. macOS may block the first launch again, as it did for 0.1.0 (see
  [Download](https://github.com/Melvin2306/pimento#download)). With Pimento sign-in, macOS asks for
  your password once so the new build can read the Keychain item. A CLI installed with *Install
  Command Line Tool…* links into the app, so it is updated with the app.
- **The command-line tool**: run the installer again (below). On Windows it now adds the
  PowerShell completions to your profile. To skip that, set `$env:PIMENTO_NO_COMPLETIONS = "1"`
  first.
- **The update check is new and on by default.** It sends one request a day to `api.github.com`,
  with no cookies, tokens or IDs. You can turn it off in *Settings › General › Updates* or with
  `PIMENTO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` (app and CLI). Demo mode never checks. The CLI checks only when you
  run `pimento version --check`.
- The first builds' flags `pimento --list`, `--dry-run` and `--tenants` still work in 0.2.x. Use
  `pimento list`, `pimento activate --dry-run` and `pimento tenants` instead.

## Download

**Mac app** (macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon and Intel):
**[Download Pimento.dmg](https://github.com/Melvin2306/pimento/releases/latest/download/Pimento.dmg)**.
It is not notarized: on first launch, allow it under **System Settings › Privacy & Security ›
Open Anyway** (macOS 15 and later) or right-click it and choose **Open** (macOS 14).

**Command-line tool only** (macOS, Linux, Windows):

```sh
# macOS and Linux: installs to ~/.local/bin, no sudo
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Melvin2306/pimento/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

```powershell
# Windows (PowerShell): installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Pimento and adds it to your PATH
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Melvin2306/pimento/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `Pimento.dmg` | the Mac app, with the CLI inside |
| `Pimento.zip` | the same app as a zip |
| `pimento-cli-macos.tar.gz` | the CLI for macOS (universal) |
| `pimento-cli-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | the CLI for Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.35+, libcurl) |
| `pimento-cli-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | the CLI for Linux arm64 (glibc 2.35+, libcurl) |
| `pimento-cli-windows-x86_64.zip` | the CLI for Windows 10/11, with PowerShell completions (needs the Visual C++ Redistributable) |

Every file is attached twice: under the stable name above and with the version in its name
(`Pimento-0.2.0.dmg`, `pimento-cli-0.2.0-macos.tar.gz`, …). The contents are identical.

## Verify

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing      # macOS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing          # Linux
gh attestation verify Pimento.dmg --repo Melvin2306/pimento   # built by this repository's release workflow
```

On Windows: `Get-FileHash pimento-cli-windows-x86_64.zip` and compare with `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The
installers check the SHA-256 (and the attestation, when the GitHub CLI is signed in) for you.
